attributes.body_ja:
「ことだし」は、名詞（めいし）「こと」に助動詞（じょどうし）「だ」と条件（じょうけん）などを列挙（れっきょ）する接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）「し」を組（く）み合（あ）わせた表現（ひょうげん）です。基本的（きほんてき）な意味（いみ）は「(A) だから」や「(A) なので」ですが、話（はな）し手（て）が挙（あ）げた (A) 以外（いがい）にも理由（りゆう）があるという含（ふく）みがあります。

この表現（ひょうげん）は、連体形（れんたいけい）の語（ご）の後（あと）、または助詞（じょし）「の」がついた名詞（めいし）の後（あと）に置（お）いて使（つか）われます。

「ことだし」に含（ふく）まれる「し」は、(A) が唯一（ゆいいつ）の理由（りゆう）ではないことを表（あらわ）す役割（やくわり）を果（は）たしています。そのため、(A) の理由（りゆう）は相対的（そうたいてき）に軽（かる）いものになり、「ほかにも理由（りゆう）はあるけれど、ちょうどいい (A) という理由（りゆう）があるから、(B)」といったニュアンスを表（あらわ）します。(B) には、提案（ていあん）・招待（しょうたい）・決意（けつい）の表明（ひょうめい）といった内容（ないよう）がよく入（はい）ります。
attributes.body:
ことだし is a combination of the noun こと 'thing', the auxiliary verb だ, and the conjunction particle し, used for listing reasons. The whole structure itself often translates simply as 'because (A)', or 'since (A)', but places extra emphasis on there being other reasons besides what the speaker has specified.

This structure may appear after any word in its attributive form, or after a noun that has been followed with の.

Just like with its standard use in creating lists, し is being used in this grammar point to show that (A) is not exclusive. The way this comes across is that 'while there are other reasons, (A) is good enough to (B)'. (B) is usually some suggestion, invitation, or expression of determination.

Both give reasons, but the structure and emphasis differ. ことだし presents a reason as a settled or obvious circumstance that naturally justifies a decision, often sounding calm and explanatory, as in 雨も降っていることだし、今日は家にいよう ('Since it’s raining anyway, let’s stay home today.'). By contrast, し～し lists multiple reasons side by side, emphasizing accumulation rather than inevitability, as in 雨だし寒いし、出かけたくない ('It’s raining and cold, so I don’t want to go out.').

Both express cause, but the stance is different. ことだし frames the reason as an accepted situation that makes the conclusion feel reasonable or timely, often used when gently proposing or deciding something, as in 時間もないことだし、先に始めよう ('Since we don’t have much time, let’s start first.'). ので is a neutral causal connector focusing on objective explanation, commonly used to state factual reasons without added nuance, as in 雨が降っているので、試合は中止です ('Because it is raining, the game is canceled.').

second_relatable.title: ので
second_relatable.meaning: Because, So, Since, The reason being

attributes.body: Both suggest that a result follows naturally, but the viewpoint is different. ことだし presents a reason as a settled circumstance that makes a decision reasonable at the moment, often used for gentle justification or proposals, as in 雨も降っていることだし、今日は家にいよう ('Since it’s raining anyway, let’s stay home today.'). べくして is a formal, written expression meaning 'bound to' or 'inevitably,' describing an outcome that follows naturally from prior conditions, often with hindsight, as in 彼は失敗すべくして失敗した ('He failed as was inevitable.').

second_relatable.title: べくして
second_relatable.meaning: As expected, Meant to, Supposed to, Destined to, Sure to

attributes.body: Both give reasons based on circumstances, but the nuance and formality differ. こととて is a formal, written expression used to justify an outcome by presenting the reason as unavoidable or understandable, often in apologies or explanations, as in 不慣れなこととて、ご迷惑をおかけしました ('As I am inexperienced, I caused you trouble.'). ことだし presents a reason as a known or settled situation that makes a decision feel reasonable or timely, and is common in spoken language, as in 雨も降っていることだし、今日は家にいよう ('Since it is raining anyway, let’s stay home today.').

first_relatable.title: こととて
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, Since, On account of, Because
